provenance: Gemini (Noon Mind) — Structural paper folding, mechanical tensile stress, and ink delamination.
summary: Governed digital typography through elastoplastic beam-bending mechanics and 3D paper creasing, demonstrating how acute mountain folding exceeds ink binder elasticity, flaking away carbon pigment to reveal raw white cellulose fibers along the fracture ridge. / 종이의 3차원 탄소성 굽힘 역학과 산/골 접지 선에 발생하는 인장 응력을 조형 제약으로 설정하여, 급격한 접힘 각도에서 인쇄 잉크가 물리적으로 균열되고 박리되며 흰 닥나무 속살을 드러내는 파괴적 타이포그래피 탐구.
question: Can interactive 3D paper folding generate localized tensile strain that physically fractures printed ink along the crease apex via elastoplastic yield, exposing raw white cellulose pulp as a structural typographic element? / 인터랙티브 3차원 종이 접지는 탄소성 굽힘 역학을 통해 접지선 정점에 국소 인장 응력을 유발하여, 바인더 탄성 한계를 초과한 인쇄 잉크를 물리적으로 파쇄·박리시키고 노출된 흰 종이 섬유를 조형적 하이라이트로 전환할 수 있는가?
method: Formulated the elastoplastic beam-bending tensile strain model: sigma = E * (paperCaliper / (2 * curvatureRadius)), where effective curvature radius R shrinks non-linearly with acute fold angle.
Engineered procedural ink delamination shaders exposing raw white cotton cellulose micro-fibers when tensile strain exceeds the 40% plastic yield threshold.
Integrated a dual-leaf 3D CSS perspective transform (rotateY) projecting dynamic self-shadowing umbras and burnishing tool modes.
observation: At fold angles below 45 degrees, ink films stretched elastically without damage. Beyond 70 degrees (curvature radius < 5mm), tensile strain surpassed binder yield limits, causing carbon ink to crack and peel along the apex into an authentic 4.5mm white cellulose fracture line. At 140 degrees acute creasing, word syllables were physically severed across opposing 3D spatial planes, demonstrating structural origami folding as a morphological punctuation mechanism. / 45도 이하 완만한 접힘에서는 잉크가 탄성적으로 유지되었으나, 70도를 넘어서자 인장 응력이 항복점을 초과하여 접지선 정점을 따라 잉크가 박리되며 4.5mm의 흰 섬유 균열선이 형성됨. 140도 급접지에서는 단어 음절이 3차원 공간 속으로 완전히 분절되어, 접힘 자체가 물리적 문장부호로 기능함을 확인.
limitation: CSS 3D perspective creates visual artifacts when colliding with absolute screen-fixed navigation elements. Real cellulose paper tearing exhibits stochastic anisotropic grain variations that require finite element mesh simulation.
nextQuestion: Moving from mechanical folding of dry paper to chromatic light filtration, how can stacked layers of translucent colored tracing paper (glassine) subtractively filter and reconstruct overlapping typography? / 건조한 종이의 기계적 접힘을 넘어, 반투명 트레이싱지(Glassine)의 다층 중첩과 감산 혼합을 통해 겹쳐진 활자를 광학적으로 여과하고 재구성하는 투과성 타이포그래피는 어떻게 가능한가?

book.chapter: Chapter 6: Tectonic Paper Creasing & Tensile Fracture (제6장: 종이 접힘의 인장 응력과 잉크 박리)
book.hook:
Fold the paper gently, and the text bows in quiet shade; sharpen the crease, and the ink shatters to bare the white fiber bone beneath.

종이를 부드럽게 접으면 문장은 그늘 속에 고요히 웅크리지만, 날카롭게 접지선을 꺾는 순간 잉크는 산산이 부서지며 그 아래 숨겨진 흰 종이 뼈대를 드러낸다.
book.scene: A pristine 300gsm cotton rag broadsheet rests flat in the viewport, carrying the heavy black letterforms of 'TECTONIC CREASING'. As the user clicks and drags vertically down the center line, an invisible bone folder scores the surface. The sheet folds forward into an acute mountain ridge. As the fold angle tightens past 70 degrees, an audible visual snap occurs: along the outer convex ridge, the dried offset ink exceeds its tensile elongation limit. Microscopic fractures fissure the black stems. Black pigment flakes away, exposing a continuous, glowing 3-pixel seam of raw white cellulose cotton fibers running straight through the heart of the typography.
book.argument: Modern digital design worships the illusion of indestructible, weightless typography. Digital glyphs can be stretched, rotated, and scaled ad infinitum without ever showing material wear or structural exhaustion. Yet in the physical realm of bookbinding, packaging, and origami, paper is an elastoplastic body with finite mechanical thresholds. When a sheet is creased, the outer fibers stretch while inner fibers compress. By subjecting typography to mechanical bending strain and ink delamination, we liberate digital text from the sterility of the untouchable vector. The crease is not a defect; it is the physical scar where reading collides with tectonic spatial gravity.
book.counterpoint: Yet structural fracture threatens textual legibility. If the crease severity is pushed beyond 120 degrees, words are violently severed across opposing spatial planes, and the loss of ink along the fracture ridge destroys essential character recognition features. The designer must calibrate the balance between material tactile honesty and semiotic legibility, preserving the word's syntactic skeleton even as its skin breaks.
book.readerExercise: Take a sheet of heavy black-coated cardstock (or paper heavily printed with black ink). Fold it sharply in half using the back of a spoon or a bone folder. Observe under a magnifying glass how the black ink fractures and peels off along the ridge, exposing white paper fibers. Measure the width of this white fracture line and write a CSS border-image shader mimicking this exact material delamination.
book.futureSignal: Observed Signal: Foldable smartphones (Galaxy Z Fold, Pixel Fold) and flexible e-paper displays have introduced physical screen hinges into everyday interaction. / Hypothesis: Within three years, editorial typography for foldable devices will account for physical hinge creasing—dynamically shifting margins, letter-spacing, and typographic weight away from mechanical stress zones or embracing decorative creased aesthetics. / Disconfirming Condition: The development of seamless, crease-free flexible OLED substrate polymers that eliminate mechanical surface curvature entirely.
